title: Who and what questions review
focus: Ask and answer bounded who-, what- and which-questions about people, things, activities and substances.
targetSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
Mikä: identifying or choosing one thing
Mitä: asking and answering about actions and objects

exercises.prompt: Write “Who are you?” in Finnish. Use olet (“you are”), sinä (“you”). Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. Kuka asks who a person is. In a neutral question, put kuka first: Kuka sinä olet? (“Who are you?”). Do not add -ko/-kö. The complete question means “Who are you”.
requiredSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
exercises.targetSkill: Kuka: asking and answering about one person

optionFeedback.Kuka sinä olet?: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. Kuka asks who a person is. In a neutral question, put kuka first: Kuka sinä olet? (“Who are you?”). Do not add -ko/-kö. The complete question means “Who are you”.

optionFeedback.Miksi sinä olet?: Choose the question word for the requested information; keep the complete intended meaning.

exercises.prompt: Translate “Minä olen lääkäri.” into English.
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. Answer from your own point of view: sinä olet (“you are”) in the question becomes minä olen (“I am”) in your reply. Hän on stays hän on when both speakers mean the same other person. Minä and sinä may be omitted with olen and olet; keep hän when referring to another person. In a role game, Kuka minä olen? (“Who am I?”) receives Sinä olet… (“You are…”), because the reply addresses the original speaker. The complete reply means “I am a doctor”.
requiredSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
exercises.targetSkill: Kuka: asking and answering about one person

exercises.prompt: Build “We are Liisa and Matti.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: When a group is addressed as te, its reply uses me olemme (“we are”). When both speakers mean another group, keep he ovat (“they are”). Profession words describing the members normally take the plural partitive: opettajia (“teachers”). The complete profession forms are provided here. In a role game, Ketkä me olemme? (“Who are we?”) receives Te olette… (“You are…” addressed to the group). The complete reply means “We are Liisa and Matti”.

exercises.prompt: Complete “Which bag is new?”: ____ laukku on uusi? Write the full sentence. Use laukku (“bag”), on (“is”), uusi (“new”). Ask about one countable thing.
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. An adjective is a word that describes a quality. Use mikä to identify one countable thing or select one item. Mikä tämä on? (“What is this?”) asks for an identity; Mikä kirja on uusi? (“Which book is new?”) selects a book. The complete question means “Which bag is new”.

exercises.prompt: Complete “What is she reading?”: ____ hän lukee? Write the full sentence. Use hän (“he or she”), lukee (“reads”).
exercises.explanation: A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. answerDiagnostics.explanation: Mikä identifies or selects one countable thing. The requested question is “Mitä hän lukee?”

exercises.prompt: Build “She is reading a newspaper.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. Answer with the corresponding activity or object, not kyllä (“yes”). Here juoda (“drink”) and syödä (“eat”) describe an unspecified amount, and lukea (“read”) describes an activity in progress, so the object uses the partitive. Use vettä (“water”), leipää (“bread”) and kirjaa (“a book”) in these bounded situations. The complete reply means “She is reading a newspaper”.

exercises.prompt: Write “What is it?” in Finnish. Use on (“is”), se (“it”). Ask about a substance.
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. Use mitä with olla when asking what a substance is: Mitä tämä on? (“What is this?” about an unidentified substance). This is why mikä with olla and mitä with other verbs is not a universal rule. The complete question means “What is it”.
